learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will learn to identify Adverbs and classify them into Adverbs of Manner, Place, Time, and Frequency.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 If Verbs are the action stars of our sentence, Adverbs are the directors! 🎬 They tell the action exactly HOW, WHEN, and WHERE it should happen. Let's discover the secret details adverbs add to our sentences!

lesson_modules.teaching_content: An Adverb is a word that modifies (adds more meaning to) a verb, an adjective, or even another adverb. Many adverbs end in '-ly', but not all of them do!
examples_or_templates: Adjective modifier: She is VERY smart.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Adverbs of Manner tell us HOW an action is done (e.g., bravely, slowly, happily). Adverbs of Place tell us WHERE an action happens (e.g., here, there, outside, upstairs).
examples_or_templates: Place: Please leave your shoes OUTSIDE.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Adverbs of Time tell us WHEN an action takes place (e.g., today, yesterday, soon). Adverbs of Frequency tell us HOW OFTEN an action happens (e.g., always, never, sometimes, usually).
examples_or_templates: Time: I will finish my homework TOMORROW.
Frequency: He ALWAYS brushes his teeth.

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Identify the Adverb of Manner in this sentence: 'The old man walked slowly across the street.'
❓ Which of these words is an Adverb of Frequency?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Turn this adjective into an adverb of manner: 'Quiet'.
subjective_practice.hint: Just add '-ly' to the end of the word.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Underline the adverb and state its kind: 'The children are playing outside.'
subjective_practice.hint: Ask yourself: Does this word tell me how, when, or where they are playing?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with an Adverb of Time: 'We are going to the zoo ________.'
subjective_practice.hint: Think of a word that means the day after today.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🎬 The Adverb Acting Challenge
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Write down a simple action like 'eating' or 'walking'. Now do it in three different ways: 'quickly', 'slowly', and 'happily'. Ask someone to guess your Adverb of Manner!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Adverbs add meaning to verbs, adjectives, and other adverbs.
⭐ Adverbs of Manner tell HOW, and Adverbs of Place tell WHERE.
⭐ Adverbs of Time tell WHEN, and Adverbs of Frequency tell HOW OFTEN.
